chunks: And Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: A man departed from ʿArafāt and passed by al-Mashʿar, but he did not stop until he reached Minā, so he cast at the Jamrah, and he did not realize it until the day had risen high.
He said: He should return to al-Mashʿar and stand there, then cast at the Jamrah.

key_terms.أَفَاضَ: departed in procession from ʿArafāt during hajj
key_terms.الْجَمْرَةَ: the Jamrah, the stoning site in Minā
key_terms.الْمَشْعَرِ: al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, the station at Muzdalifah where one stands during hajj
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: the plain of ʿArafāt, a principal station of hajj
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the location where pilgrims perform rites including the stoning
key_terms.يَرْمِي: he casts, meaning he throws the pebbles in the rite
key_terms.يَقِفُ: he stands, referring here to the ritual standing

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if he misses standing at al-Mashʿar and reaches Minā before realizing it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who left ʿArafāt, passed al-Mashʿar without الوقوف, and proceeded to Minā. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام instructs that he must return to al-Mashʿar, perform the standing there, and then cast at the Jamrah, showing the required order of these hajj rites.
